item.text: {"question_id":"4B.7","answer":"During 2023, Scholz’s coalition pursued several inclusion measures: it ended discriminatory blood-donation exclusions for gay, bisexual, and trans people; extended temporary protection and associated work and social access for people fleeing Ukraine; made all asylum seekers eligible for integration courses; strengthened disability-employment penalties from 2024; ratified the ILO Violence and Harassment Convention; and advanced a draft self-determination law for trans, intersex, and nonbinary people [BATCH-0001-E006, BATCH-0008-E004, BATCH-0011-R01-E006, BATCH-0009-E019, BATCH-0008-E011, BATCH-0008-E006]. It also funded diversity and anti-extremism organizations and amended the Federal Expellees Act to ease proof of status for Spätaussiedler applicants [BATCH-0009-E018, BATCH-0033-E025]. These measures did not establish consistently equal practical access. The promised expansion of the Anti-Discrimination Act had not been enacted by the reporting deadline; disability-access requirements were inconsistently enforced; eligible third-country nationals under temporary protection were sometimes denied registration or pressured into asylum procedures and received less favorable work and benefit access; and vulnerability identification and support for asylum seekers remained unsystematic, with implementation and monitoring varying across Länder [BATCH-0008-E002, BATCH-0011-R01-E008, BATCH-0011-R03-E002]. Educational access also varied materially by region: some Länder delayed school enrollment by one to two months or restricted access to regular schooling, while federal-state rules strongly affected participation [BATCH-0011-R04-E018]. In late 2023, some pro-Palestinian demonstrations were prohibited without distinction as to their cause, which the report characterized as violating equal freedom of assembly; police responses were criticized as partly racially motivated [BATCH-0011-R04-E006]. Minority-targeted harms also remained substantial: attacks on migrants, asylum seekers, and refugees rose from 1,371 in 2022 to 1,515 in 2023, while recorded anti-LSBTIQ* crimes rose to 1,785, although underreporting and increased reporting complicate trend and policy-effectiveness inferences [BATCH-0011-R04-E015, BATCH-0003-E006, BATCH-0003-E007]. The self-determination bill itself remained contested: the Bundesrat and experts raised concerns about minors’ rights, parental consent, data protection, and possible deterrence, while the federal government rejected key criticisms [BATCH-0034-R04-E004, BATCH-0034-R04-E005]. Overall, the evidence supports meaningful federal inclusion efforts alongside persistent unequal access and restrictions affecting excluded groups and unpopular viewpoints. Attribution is generally to the coalition government, federal agencies, Länder, or municipalities; the supplied evidence does not establish Scholz’s personal direction, and several outcomes depended substantially on subnational implementation.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0001-E006","BATCH-0008-E004","BATCH-0011-R01-E006","BATCH-0009-E019","BATCH-0008-E011","BATCH-0008-E006","BATCH-0009-E018","BATCH-0033-E025"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0008-E002","BATCH-0011-R01-E008","BATCH-0011-R03-E002","BATCH-0011-R04-E018","BATCH-0011-R04-E006","BATCH-0011-R04-E015","BATCH-0003-E006","BATCH-0003-E007","BATCH-0034-R04-E004","BATCH-0034-R04-E005"],"limitations_and_gaps":["The supplied evidence does not provide a comprehensive measure of equal political participation for women, minorities, opposition regions, or unpopular viewpoints.","Several favorable measures were proposals, drafts, or laws whose implementation began after 2023;
